findings.title: `<%- end if %>` is a Ruby syntax error; the embed view can never render
findings.body: The ERb at line 6 reads `<%- end if %>` with no condition following the `if` modifier. When ERb compiles the template the generated Ruby ends with `end if`, which is a syntax error (unexpected end-of-input). Any request to /embed/best for which a TopicEmbed exists (the main success path of this feature) will raise ActionView::Template::Error instead of rendering the comments. The controller specs never render views (TopicView is mocked, no render_views), so CI does not catch this — a view-rendering test is needed.

findings.title: Stored XSS: embed URL interpolated unescaped into raw HTML footer
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import builds the "Imported from" footer with `"#{url}"` — the URL is interpolated into HTML with no escaping, and the resulting post is stored with cook_method raw_html (cooked = raw, bypassing the sanitizing Markdown pipeline) and rendered in app/views/embed/best.html.erb with `raw post.cooked`. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?:///`, which permits quotes, `>`, and attribute-breaking characters. An attacker can hit /embed/best with a crafted embed_url whose host matches embeddable_host (e.g. `http:///?'>

findings.title: RSS item content imported as raw_html with no sanitization — stored XSS from feed content
findings.body: poll_feed passes `i.content` (the raw HTML from the feed's content:encoded/body) straight into TopicEmbed.import, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Post#cook then returns the raw string untouched, skipping the normal cooking/sanitizing pipeline, and best.html.erb renders it with `raw post.cooked`. Anyone who can influence the feed's HTML (compromised or malicious feed source at the admin-configured feed_polling_url) gets arbitrary JavaScript executed on the Discourse origin for every viewer, including logged-in staff. The readability path at least whitelists tags/attributes; the feed path has no equivalent. The imported HTML should be run through a sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize with a whitelist) before being stored as raw_html.

findings.title: absolutize_urls raises URI::InvalidURIError for URLs that pass the http(s) regex
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import only gates on `url =~ /^https?:///`, but absolutize_urls then calls `URI(url)` which raises URI::InvalidURIError for URLs containing spaces or other invalid characters (e.g. `http://exa mple.com/post` or an unencoded `%zz`). Unlike TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, there is no rescue here, so a single malformed feed link (or a crafted embed_url) raises an unhandled exception. In PollFeed this aborts the remaining feed items; in RetrieveTopic the job fails. The URI parse should be guarded or the URL rejected up front with a full URI parse.

findings.title: Nil or failing feed item aborts the entire feed import with no per-item error handling
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every RSS/Atom item has content; for plain RSS 2.0 feeds without content:encoded, simple-rss returns nil for `i.content`, so this line raises NoMethodError on the first such item and the whole poll is aborted. Similarly, any exception raised while importing one item (bad URL, PostCreator failure — note that if the post fails to save, TopicEmbed.import still calls TopicEmbed.create! with a nil topic_id, raising RecordInvalid inside the transaction) prevents all subsequent items from being imported. Each item should be processed with its own error handling (and nil content handled, e.g. falling back to i.description).

findings.title: request.referer interpolated into a JS string literal without escape_javascript
findings.body: The layout does `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. The referer is only validated to have a host equal to embeddable_host; its path/query can contain arbitrary characters (an attacker can send a request with a crafted Referer header directly — no control of a page on the host is needed). The value is placed in a single-quoted JavaScript string with no `j`/escape_javascript; it currently survives only because Rails' HTML escaping converts quotes to `'`, which then appears literally inside the script block, producing an invalid targetOrigin that makes postMessage throw a SyntaxError and breaks iframe resizing for such referers. It should be escaped with escape_javascript (and ideally the exact origin, not the full referer, used as targetOrigin).

findings.title: Feed and page fetches use open() with no timeout; a slow source hangs the job and the hourly schedule
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (and `open(url)` in TopicEmbed.import_remote) use Kernel#open with no read/open timeout. The scheduled job has `retry: false` and is also invoked synchronously from TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve on a user-triggered retrieve, so a hanging or very slow feed server blocks a Sidekiq worker indefinitely and stalls subsequent scheduled runs. open-uri should be given `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` (or a job-level timeout).

findings.title: setnx/expire are not atomic; a crash between them permanently disables retrieval for a URL
findings.body: retrieved_recently? performs `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)`. If the process dies between the two calls (or the expire fails), the key exists with no TTL and the URL is considered 'recently retrieved' forever — the embed will never be fetched again through the throttled path, leaving the loading page reloading every 30 seconds indefinitely. A single SET key 1 EX 60 NX (or a Lua script) should be used instead.

findings.title: embed_url column is varchar(255); real URLs (plus the appended footer) can exceed it
findings.body: The embed_url column is a Rails `string`, i.e. varchar(255) on PostgreSQL, with a NOT NULL constraint. Web page URLs frequently exceed 255 characters, and TopicEmbed.import additionally embeds the URL twice (href and text) into the post body; an over-long feed link will make the INSERT fail with 'value too long for type character varying(255)', aborting the import. The column should be text (or a larger limit) to match how URLs are stored elsewhere.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching instead of exact origin comparison
findings.body: The resize handler accepts messages when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is false, i.e. when the message origin appears anywhere as a substring of discourseUrl. That is not an equality check: any origin that happens to occur inside the discourseUrl string (e.g. as part of a path, or a shorter scheme/host prefix in some configurations) is accepted, and e.data.height is used unvalidated. The consequence is limited to resizing the iframe, but the check should compare `e.origin` against the exact expected origin (e.g. the parsed origin of discourseUrl) and the height coerced to a positive integer.

findings.title: `force: true` added to an existing migration will drop an already-created top_topics table
findings.body: This PR changes the previously shipped CreateTopTopics migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. With force: true, create_table drops the table if it already exists; any environment that already ran the original migration and then re-runs it (db:migrate:redo, rebuilding from migrations rather than schema.rb) will silently lose all top_topics data. If the change was needed for test databases, it should be made in a separate migration or the test schema rebuilt, not by editing a released migration.

findings.title: Only Gemfile_rails4.lock was updated; the default (Rails 3) lockfile is missing the new gems
findings.body: The PR adds ruby-readability and simple-rss to the Gemfile and updates Gemfile_rails4.lock, but the repository's dual-boot setup (see the Bundler monkey patch at the top of the Gemfile) uses the default Gemfile.lock when booting in Rails 3 mode (`RAILS3` set), which per the diff was not regenerated. Any Rails 3-mode CI run or deployment will fail to resolve the new dependencies (TopicEmbed/poll_feed require them at runtime), so the Rails 3 lockfile needs the corresponding entries.
